findings.title: Plugin request logs no longer include traceID
findings.body: The previous logRequest implementation explicitly extracted traceID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext and appended it to the log fields. The refactored code removes that logic, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only adds endpoint, pluginId, datasource, and user fields. There is no replacement in this change, so plugin request logs emitted by LoggerMiddleware may lose trace correlation.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards captured logs and context
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware now logs through logger.FromContext(ctx). The test fake responds by returning a brand-new TestLogger, so messages logged through the contextual logger are not recorded on the original fake and contextual state is lost. This makes it difficult or impossible to assert log output from code paths that use FromContext and can hide regressions in tests.

findings.title: NewMetricsMiddleware mutates a shared middleware instance
findings.body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates a single *MetricsMiddleware and the returned ClientMiddlewareFunc sets imw.next = next each time it is applied. If the same middleware value is used to wrap more than one client, or is applied concurrently, the next field can be overwritten, causing requests to be forwarded to the wrong client or creating a data race. Middleware constructors should create a new wrapper per application or avoid mutable shared state.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to Logger is an interface break
findings.body: The exported Logger interface now requires FromContext(context.Context) Logger. Any existing implementation of this interface outside this package will fail to compile until updated, making this change a backward-incompatible API change.

findings.title: No tests verify the new contextual logger enrichment
findings.body: The PR introduces a middleware whose purpose is to enrich the request context and changes LoggerMiddleware to depend on that enrichment, but there are no tests verifying that QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, or CollectMetrics contexts receive the expected attributes or that LoggerMiddleware logs them. Given the fake logger's FromContext currently discards contextual logs, this behavior can regress silently.
